summary: The 13-file budget exactly covers the committed OIDC/browser facade, its safe audit event vocabulary, package declaration, and focused tests; no unrelated surface is admitted.
current_flow: Hosted OIDC and browser-auth trust boundaries are implemented and validated. Browser callbacks use a state cookie, operations workers reject browser auth routes before authentication parsing, and public UI remains deferred to its dedicated stage.

criteria_map.Generic OIDC validates discovery issuer,: oidc-adapter.ts owns discovery, PKCE/token exchange, JWKS validation, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce checks using constrained transport.
criteria_map.Public local and hosted auth routes cons: browser-auth.ts consumes opaque local and browser credentials through Stage 2 helpers and repository atomic consumption.
criteria_map.Hosted identity is keyed by issuer plus: browser-auth.ts uses durable identity, grant, invitation, session, rotation, and reauthentication repository methods.
criteria_map.Only the full Control profile mounts UI: index.ts and ui-static.ts mount browser routes and UI only in the full profile.

rounds.question: Should the event vocabulary be omitted to preserve an arbitrary 12-file limit?

citations.finding: Browser authentication requires secret-free audit events and profile-bound routing.
